prompts.dry: Use case: stylized-concept. Production sprite concept atlas for Doom II. All four supplied images are direct style references (TRE1 dead snag, TRE2 gnarled tree, SMIT broken stump, SMT2 broken taper shape). Match their original coarse dirty hand-pixeled 1994 appearance, muddy olive-brown palette, limited shading steps, small irregular highlight clusters and angular contours. NO modern smooth fantasy illustration, no 3D render, no polished wood, no faces, no spherical holes, no leafy foliage, no giant roots. Exactly SIX isolated subjects on uniform pure #FF00FF magenta including all inner gaps, without text, numbers, borders, ground, shadows or grid. Canvas 1536x1024: top row three separate trees centered around x256,768,1280, all above y650, each about 560px tall with clear margins; bottom row three MUCH SHORTER stumps around y840 about 190px tall. Subjects may not touch or overlap their neighbors. Sprite front projection with modest fixed upper-left highlights. Crisp low resolution pixel art, nearest-neighbor enlargement, logical pixel ~5 output pixels, details no smaller than a logical pixel. Each family has three distinct tree and stump shapes. This is an alternative design proposal, not an upscale of the references. APPROACH C: FRACTURED AND WEATHERED. This alternative should feel battered, ancient and harsh, with dry splintered breaks and brittle black twig ends, NOT smoothly twisted ornamental trees. Match TRE1's black/gray weathering over ochre-brown bark and the original granular Doom pixel density. Tree A has a snapped top and three short sharp branch remnants. Tree B is squat and irregularly crooked with one dead horizontal bough and small broken branch clusters. Tree C is taller, forked, one side snapped with a narrow vertical split; no giant decorative hole. Stumps A/B/C: thin sharply broken spike, low shattered stump with jagged top, uneven split stump with a small dark split inside. Muted charcoal-gray crust and dry dull brown exposed wood; no glowing embers, no frost, no rust-red ground. Compact roots; grain made of irregular tiny pixel clusters, no clean ruled vertical stripes.
prompts.charred: Use case: style-transfer. Edit the supplied APPROVED STYLE C Doom sprite atlas to create one environmental material variant. This is the binding style and design reference. Preserve ALL SIX exact tree/stump designs, their positions, sizes, branch courses, root footprints, jagged broken tips and small pixel-cluster bark texture. Keep the three trees top row and three MUCH SMALLER stumps bottom row, 1536x1024 canvas. Maintain original Doom II low-resolution gritty pixel realism and enlarged crisp square pixels. Preserve the broken weathered wood anatomy and modest fixed upper-left highlights. No smoother redraw, no polished 3D-rendered texture, no decorative faces or new holes, no extra branches, no scenery, ground, shadows, labels, borders or text. Keep an absolutely flat pure #FF00FF chroma-magenta background everywhere outside the six objects and inside all gaps. Objects remain separated. Change only the surface material/color as specified. Do not tint the background. DEEP CARBON: Near-black carbonized bark across all six objects, very restrained deep gray midtone clusters and narrow broken gray edge highlights that retain readable volume. Only a trace of brown inside deepest broken wood. Rough fragmented grain like original Doom, not flat black silhouettes. This is the darkest option but still discernible against a dark game wall. No fire, glowing cracks, smoke, snow or new geometry.
